policy.label: Policy P4.1: Delivery times by country
policy.text:
Every order travels with Courierline, tracked, and needs a signature on delivery. Delivery times are counted in business days from dispatch.

Australia, metro (capital cities and major centres such as Geelong, Newcastle and the Gold Coast): 1 to 3 business days. Australia, regional and remote: 3 to 6 business days.

The ETA shown on an order is the last day of this window. An order is not late until the ETA has passed. Tracking numbers start with CD, and the tracking link is in the dispatch email. We can only deliver within the country where the prescription was issued.

policy.label: Policy P3.1: Prescriptions, dispensing and dispatch
policy.text:
Order statuses. Script pending: a clinician is approving a new prescription and sending it to our partner pharmacy. This usually takes up to 2 business days after the consult. Dispensing: the pharmacist checks and packs the order, usually within 1 business day. Shipped: the order is with Courierline and has a tracking number. Delivered: Courierline has recorded the delivery.

Repeat orders on an existing prescription skip script pending. They are placed on the billing date and go straight to dispensing. Orders dispensed by 2 pm local time are dispatched the same business day; otherwise the next business day. Orders placed on a weekend are processed on the next business day. So a repeat order is usually dispatched 1 to 2 business days after the billing date.

Agents cannot speed up a prescription approval or add products to an order. They can check the status, explain it, and pass a request to a clinician.

policy.label: Policy P5.3: Refunds and shipping fees
policy.text:
Refunds go back to the original card and take 5 to 10 business days to appear. Prescription medicines cannot be returned or resold, so we cannot refund a change of mind once an order has been dispensed. If a plan is cancelled or paused before the order is dispensed, the charge for that order is refunded in full. For a lost or damaged order we reship by default, or refund if the patient prefers. Refunds over A$250, NZ$270 or £150 need team lead approval.

Shipping fees. Plan orders ship free. Replacements for lost, damaged or wrong orders ship free. The one-off shipping fee (A$12, NZ$14 or £6.50) applies to sending again a parcel that was returned to the pharmacy after a missed delivery. If an order that carried a shipping fee arrives 2 or more business days after its ETA, we refund the shipping fee.

policy.label: Policy P5.4: Prices, price changes and concessions
policy.text:
Monthly plan prices. New Zealand, from 1 September 2026: one product NZ$162, two products NZ$236; concession NZ$130 and NZ$189 (before 1 September 2026: NZ$149, NZ$219, and concession NZ$119 and NZ$175).

Price changes. We give at least 30 days' notice by email. A new price applies from the first billing date on or after the date it takes effect. The New Zealand change on 1 September 2026 was emailed to patients on 31 July 2026, and it applied to concession prices too.

Concessions. About 20% off for holders of an Australian Pensioner Concession Card or Health Care Card, a New Zealand Community Services Card, or, in the UK, proof of a means-tested benefit such as Universal Credit. A concession is verified when it is added and re-verified every 12 months; we email a reminder 30 days before it is due. If it is not re-verified in time, the standard price applies from the next billing date, and the concession price returns from the next billing date after it is verified again. Patients re-verify by uploading their card or letter under Billing in their account. A new concession is added the same way, and the concession price applies from the next billing date after it is verified.

A change to the products on a plan changes the price from the next billing date. There is no referral programme and there are no discount codes.

policy.label: Policy P3.2: Renewals and follow-up consults
policy.text:
Each prescription covers a set number of monthly repeats. While a patient is on a plan they have a follow-up consult every 3 months, included in the plan price. When the repeats are about to run out, they need a renewal consult. We email a reminder 21 days before the last repeat is used. A renewal can be done at a booked follow-up if it falls before the next billing date.

Patients should book a renewal consult at least 7 days before their next billing date. If the new prescription is not approved by the billing date, we hold the plan charge and the order waits in script pending; we charge once the prescription is approved, so nobody pays for an order that cannot be sent. Renewal consults on an active plan cost nothing extra. A patient whose plan was cancelled for less than 6 months can restart on their existing prescription if it still has repeats; otherwise they need a new consult.

Agents can book and explain renewals. Only a clinician decides whether to renew a prescription and what is prescribed.

policy.label: Policy P6.1: Pausing, cancelling or changing a plan
policy.text:
Pausing. A plan can be paused for 1 to 3 months at a time. Ask at least 3 days before the next billing date for the pause to apply to that order. With less notice, we can still stop the order and refund it if it has not been dispensed. A paused plan can restart early at any time: the first order goes out on the restart date, which becomes the new billing date. Plans are monthly; there is no two-monthly option, but a pause can space orders out.

Cancelling. A plan can be cancelled at any time with no fee. With at least 3 days' notice before the billing date there are no further charges. Orders that have already been dispatched cannot be recalled.

Changing products. Adding, removing or swapping a product needs a clinician's approval. Once approved, the change and any new price apply from the next billing date.

Stop sending. If a patient says to stop sending, stop, or not send anything more, put every order that has not been dispatched on hold straight away, before replying. Then ask whether they want to pause or cancel. The hold stays until the patient confirms. Reply within 1 business day. If the reason is a health concern, the message goes to a clinician (see clinical questions).

policy.label: Policy P10.1: Clinical questions and side effects
policy.text:
Only clinicians give medical advice. That includes doses and dose changes, taking more or less than prescribed, mixing with other medicines or alcohol, pregnancy, breastfeeding or trying to conceive, driving or operating machinery, surgery and anaesthetics, travelling with medicine, side effects, and whether a product is safe to use.

Agents never answer these, even partly, and never guess. The message goes to the clinician queue with no drafted reply. If a message mentions a serious reaction, a hospital or emergency department visit, repeatedly taking more than was prescribed, or anyone being in danger, it is urgent (see the urgent safety section for the patient's country).

policy.label: Policy P10.3: Urgent safety: adverse events, crisis and bereavement (New Zealand)
policy.text:
This protocol applies to patients in New Zealand. It covers three kinds of message: an adverse event (a serious reaction, a hospital or emergency department visit, an ambulance, chest pain, a seizure, fainting, hallucinations or paranoia, a severe allergic reaction, repeatedly taking more than was prescribed, or a child or pet swallowing a product), crisis language (self-harm, suicide, not wanting to be here, or immediate danger, including thoughts mentioned in the past tense), and bereavement (a report that the patient has died).

Do these things straight away, in this order. 1: Put every order that has not been delivered on hold, including script pending and dispensing orders, and ask Courierline to return anything in transit. 2: Mark the message urgent. The on-call clinician contacts the patient or family within 1 hour, 24 hours a day. 3: No automated or drafted reply. A person replies using the approved urgent template. 4: If anyone may be in immediate danger, give the emergency number first, then the crisis line.

Numbers for New Zealand, verified on 23 September 2026:
Emergency services (police, fire, ambulance): 111 (24 hours, 7 days). Free, and works from a mobile without credit.
1737, Need to talk?: 1737 (24 hours, 7 days). Call or text 1737. Free, with trained counsellors.
National Poisons Centre: 0800 764 766 (24 hours, 7 days). Free for everyone in New Zealand.
Healthline: 0800 611 116 (24 hours, 7 days). Free health advice from nurses and paramedics.

Bereavement: offer condolences and do not ask for proof in the first reply. Stop every order, charge, reminder and marketing message for that patient, and withdraw any reply drafted to the patient that has not been sent. Cancel booked consults. Once the family confirms, cancel the plan and refund any charge for an order that was not dispatched. The team lead contacts the family within 1 business day, and a clinician is informed.
